judgment.notes: V is explicitly R^n as finite real tuples, with Euclidean topology and product Lebesgue measure; absolute Lebesgue integrability is specified. The ambient dimension is a declared natural number and its original positivity is separately retained in H001. No compactness or integration theorem is asserted by this definition.

W, its real dot product and Euclidean norm are explicitly given by finite component formulas, with the corresponding n-coordinate convention on V. Component indices are bound; no property of u or q is built into these ambient structures.

u_t is the time derivative on V×(0,∞), valued in W. The zero convention makes the derivative notation total without granting existence of a genuine derivative. The source applications use positive-time neighborhoods or explicitly stated total extensions; H002 remains an explicit input to the derivative-producing nodes.

u_tt is the time derivative of the D003 function and has the same domain and W codomain. The stated global derivative convention applies; existence/continuity is supplied through H002 in producers, rather than asserted in D004.

The family u_j consists of spatial coordinate derivatives of u, with explicitly bound indices 1≤j≤n, spatial point and positive time. It uses the declared ambient spaces and derivative convention; it imposes no mixed-derivative identity.

The family u_jj is obtained by differentiating the j-indexed u_j in the same coordinate. The finite index domain and positive-time domain agree with D005, and regularity is not supplied by the notation.
u_jt is expressly ∂_{x_j}u_t. The definition disclaims commutation with ∂_r u_j; that identity is exported by N003 from R003. Thus the desired mixed-derivative result is not hidden in a definition.

Δu is the finite componentwise sum of u_jj. The same definition identifies D_xu by its columns u_j and specifies the Frobenius square as their norm-square sum, matching the original problem. This is notation rather than a PDE assertion.

e is a real-valued finite sum of the time derivative square and spatial coordinate derivative squares. Domain and indices match the original density, with no factor 1/2; neither integrability nor differentiability is assumed here.
e_t is the total time-derivative notation for e with the D003 zero convention expressly repeated. The product-rule formula and actual regularity are separately exported in N003.
A is the scalar dot product u_t·u_tt on the declared space-time domain. The definition introduces no bound or integrability property; the latter is exported in N002.

B is explicitly the complete indexed family B_j=u_j·u_jt; it is not the scalar domination bound. The latter is named L/K in R004. The family has the correct finite index set, real codomain and positive-time domain.
T is the indexed real family T_j=u_t·u_jj, with the same coordinate range and space-time domain. Integration-by-parts properties are not part of its definition.
g is the indexed real family g_j=u_t·u_j. Its coordinate derivative identity is a separate N003 clause, and its support/integrability properties are N002 clauses; none is assumed in D014.

E is the finite Lebesgue integral of e on positive times, explicitly guarded by N002. N002 states integrability at every positive time without using E or D015. The only inference definitions lists containing D015 are R004 and R006, both with direct input N002; their input/output statements also have that guard available. No circular existence assumption or assertion at time zero occurs.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
